subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can definite integrals be set up and evaluated to find geometric areas bounded by curves and coordinate lines?
in_scope_units: 8.1 Introduction: limits of elementary geometry for curved boundaries.
8.2 Area under Simple Curves: vertical and horizontal strips, signed integrals and areas bounded by standard curves.
Exercise 8.1 and Miscellaneous Examples: circles, ellipses, parabolas, lines and trigonometric curves.
Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 8: area problems requiring graphing and interval splitting.

known_pitfalls.claim: A definite integral below the x-axis is already the positive area.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is negative; geometric area uses its absolute value.

known_pitfalls.claim: The area of a curve crossing the axis can be found with one unsplit signed integral.
known_pitfalls.correction: For geometric area, split at each crossing and add absolute values.
Horizontal strips may be easier when x is naturally a function of y.

known_pitfalls.claim: Symmetry changes the equation of the curve.
known_pitfalls.correction: Symmetry only reduces the region that must be integrated; the same curve equation remains.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 1 to derive the area pi a^2 of a circle.
Use NCERT Example 2 to derive the area pi ab of an ellipse.
Use NCERT Example 3 to split the area for y=3x+2 across the x-axis.
Use NCERT Example 4 for the area under y=cos x from 0 to 2pi.
Use the Miscellaneous Exercise to practise graph-first interval selection.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercise 8.1 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 8.
